content: The following are detailed precautionary statements and guidelines for pesticide products, categorized by their potential hazards and risks: Livestock Pesticides can be dangerous or harmful to domestic animals and wildlife. Livestock should be removed from the area before treatment. After treatment, livestock must be kept out of treated areas for a specified period (e.g., hours or days). Aquatic Organisms Pesticides are dangerous or harmful to fish. Avoid contaminating water sources with the product or its container. Do not clean application equipment near surface water, and prevent contamination through farmyard or road drains. To protect aquatic organisms, non-target plants, and insects, maintain an unsprayed buffer zone of a specified distance from non-agricultural land or surface water bodies. Groundwater To protect groundwater, do not apply the product more than the specified frequency or time period. This chemical may leach into groundwater, especially in areas with permeable soils or shallow water tables. Birds and Mammals Pesticides can be dangerous or harmful to birds and mammals. Do not apply pesticides during the bird breeding period. To protect birds and wild mammals, the product must be fully incorporated into the soil. Treated seeds, granules, pellets, or baits left exposed on the soil surface may pose a hazard to birds and wildlife. Any spills during loading should be covered or collected. Honey Bees Pesticides are dangerous to bees. To protect bees and other pollinators, avoid applying pesticides to flowering crops or areas where bees are actively foraging. Remove or cover beehives during application and for a specified time afterward. Do not apply pesticides when flowering weeds are present; remove weeds before flowering. Storage Pesticide storage areas must be locked and secure to prevent vandalism, with precautionary signs posted. Always store pesticides in their original containers. If a container leaks, place it in another container and clearly label the outer container. Storage areas should be dry, well-lit, and ventilated, and kept clean. Spills must be cleaned up promptly. Herbicides, insecticides, and fungicides should be stored in separate areas within the storage unit. Disposal Disposal instructions depend on the pesticide and its formulation and must be specified by the manufacturer and approved by the competent authority. Do not reuse pesticide containers for any purpose. Return empty containers to the supplier. Improper disposal of pesticide waste, spray mixtures, or rinsate is a violation of national law. Contact the appropriate government entity for guidance if disposal cannot follow label instructions. Waste from pesticide use must be disposed of at an approved waste disposal facility. Empty containers should be triple-rinsed, and the rinsate sprayed over treated fields. Treated Seeds Treated seeds must not be used for human or animal consumption or processing. Keep them out of reach of children, livestock, and wildlife. Handle seed packages carefully, avoid skin and respiratory contact, and wear protective equipment during handling and equipment cleaning. Wash hands and exposed skin before meals and after work. Avoid leaving treated seeds near surface water and clean up any spillages. Do not treat previously treated seeds with additional products. Sowing should follow the recommended seeding rate. Treated seeds must be covered with soil, including at row ends, to protect birds and mammals. After Sowing Do not leave empty seed bags or leftover treated seeds in the environment. Dispose of them according to local legislation. Return leftover treated seeds to their original bags, and do not reuse empty seed bags for other purposes. Baits Remove any bait spillages immediately. Baits must be securely placed to minimize the risk of consumption by non-target animals. Secure bait blocks to prevent rodents from dragging them away. Mark the treatment area during the treatment period. Remove dead rodents daily and dispose of them properly, avoiding refuse bins or rubbish tips. All baits must be removed after treatment is completed. Equipment Care Application equipment must be kept in good condition, free from leaks and external contamination. Clean equipment regularly. Hazard Color Bands Hazard color bands, based on acute toxicity classifications, should be printed horizontally at the bottom of the label. The color bands correspond to specific hazard levels, such as red for highly toxic products or green for low-hazard products. The classification system (GHS or WHO) used in a country should determine the color bands, but the two systems should not be mixed. Pictograms Pictograms should be printed in black and white and placed at the bottom of the label. Their size should be appropriate for the label, with a preferred size of 15 mm x 15 mm for bottles of 1 to 5 liters. Pictograms must align with the specific safety precautions for the product. Pictograms should distinguish between handling the concentrate and applying the product. For example, gloves and eye protection may be required when handling the concentrate, while boots may be necessary during application. Environmental warning pictograms, if needed, should appear to the right of the wash after use pictogram. Supplementary Information Pesticide distributors and retailers should provide users with information about the meaning of pictograms on labels. This information can be distributed as brochures, leaflets, or laminated cards in the language(s) understood by users. These materials can also be included in pesticide packaging.
